text:
Olivia Chen: FYI customer acme-inc reporting 403s immediately after our scheduled API key rotation (02:10 UTC). Ticket SUP-2189. Only affecting their web tier behind our sidecar proxy. Logs show key in header doesn't match vault record. Repro below.

Samir Patel: Do we know if the sidecar hot-reloads env vars or if it reads from a file at start? Could be stale env.

Olivia Chen: Quick repro I ran from their env:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: ApiKey OLD_KEY_VALUE" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
# HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
# {"error":"unauthorized","code":"KEY_REVOKED"}
```
Shows the app / sidecar still sending the old key.

ops-bot: Vault rotation event recorded: secret acme/api-key rotated at 2026-03-17T02:10:05Z, origin=scheduled-rotation, operator=rotation-service.

Richard Gomez: Sidecar version in that cluster (eu-prod) is 1.18. Our older sidecar reads key from mounted file at startup and caches it in memory; it only re-reads on SIGHUP or restart. If their deployment didn't roll, it would keep old key.

Maya Li: @Samir can you check the k8s rollout history for acme web deployment? If the configmap annotation checksum didn't change, kube won't restart pods.

Samir Patel: Checked: deployment/acme-web has no checksum annotation update and last rollout was 2026-03-16T22:05:11Z. Sidecar image was unchanged. So pods didn't restart.

Olivia Chen: I tried a targeted fix: restarted 3 web pods in eu-prod and sidecars picked up new key. Most requests succeeded after that, but customer still sees sporadic 403s from one edge node (eu-west-1).

Richard Gomez: Could be an edge cache that stores the old key->session mapping. We have short-lived edge auth cache that expires in 5m by default but if TTL skewed during rotation some nodes can hold stale entries longer.

Samir Patel: Mitigation options: (1) Force restart of all pods in the deployment to purge in-memory caches; (2) Invalidate edge auth cache (we have an admin purge endpoint); (3) Temporarily enable grace acceptance for old key — but that widens blast radius.

Olivia Chen: I attempted (2) via admin purge: POST https://edge-admin.redwood-inference.com/purge-auth with body {"tenant":"acme-inc"} — got 200 on most control plane nodes but one returned 504.

support-bot: Support ticket updated: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/SUP-2189 — status: investigating, priority: high.

Maya Li: I can take edge cache purge + follow up to ops. @Richard can you open a quick runbook PR to document sidecar hot-reload behavior and a kube-annotation to force pod restarts on secret change?

Richard Gomez: On it. Suggested immediate kubectl command to force rollout (safe, single-line):
```bash
kubectl -n acme patch deployment acme-web -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rotatedAt":"$(date -u +%s)"}}}}}'
```
This bumps pod template and forces a restart so the sidecar reloads file on start.

Samir Patel: Also adding a short-term alert: detect mismatch between vault.Lookup(key_id) and incoming header key hash for the same tenant — we should auto-open an incident if >1% of requests are 403 after a rotation window.

Olivia Chen: Customer accepted a coordinated window. I performed full rollout and edge purge; they confirmed success for 95% of traffic. One long-lived client still hit a 403, they said client app restarted only every ~12h. We'll ask them to restart.

Maya Li: Action items:
- Richard: PR runbook + add annotation pattern to secret controller (due EOD).
- Samir: Add alert rule for auth mismatch (P0).
- Olivia: Update ticket SUP-2189 with timeline and mitigation steps; confirm customer restart.

Olivia Chen: Closing thread here; will re-open if any residual 403s. Thanks all :thumbsup:
